blocks.en: The prose that ships alongside the type sketch. One page. Sentence-case headings, no boilerplate. Replace the italic notes with actual content.
blocks.zh: 与类型草图一起交付的说明，一页。标题采用 sentence case，不写套话。将斜体提示替换为实际内容。

blocks.en: *One paragraph. What we're trying to do, and what about the existing system or constraints makes the shape non-obvious. If [Phase A](../SKILL.md#phase-a-ground-the-problem) surfaced constraints the design must honor (existing types to interop with, callers we can't break, invariants that crossed our boundary), name them here so the reader sees the same constraints you saw.*
blocks.zh: *一段。说明想做什么，以及现有系统或约束为何使设计形态不显然。如果 [Phase A](../SKILL.md#phase-a-ground-the-problem) 发现设计必须遵守的约束（须互操作的现有类型、不能破坏的调用方、跨越边界的不变量），在这里列明，让读者看到与你相同的约束。*

blocks.en: *Write this first, before the type sketch. Show the README or quickstart the consumer reads, plus two or three realistic call sites in their own code. What they import, what they call, what comes back. The type sketch in [Shape](#shape) is derived from this. The two must agree. When they diverge, reconcile the sketch to the usage, not the reverse. The caller's experience is the spec. The types serve it.*
blocks.zh: *先写这里，再画类型草图。展示使用者会读的 README 或 quickstart，以及他们代码中两三个真实调用点：导入什么、调用什么、返回什么。[形态](#shape) 一节的类型草图由此派生，两者必须一致。冲突时调整草图去适应使用方式，而非反过来。调用方体验就是规范，类型为它服务。*

blocks.en: *The recommended architecture. Data structures first. Then how data flows through the signatures. Name the load-bearing decisions. State which invariants are encoded in types, where validation lives, and what the system deliberately does not do. Judge interface depth explicitly. State what complexity the public surface hides, what remains exposed to callers, and why the interface is no larger than needed. Cite the principle behind each decision (e.g., `per boundary-discipline`). Don't restate it.*
blocks.zh: *推荐架构。先数据结构，再说明数据如何经过函数签名流动。点明关键设计决定，说明哪些不变量编码在类型中、校验放哪里、系统有意不做什么。明确评价接口深度：公共接口隐藏什么复杂性、哪些仍暴露给调用方、为什么接口没有超出需要。每项决策引用其原则（如 `per boundary-discipline`），不重述原则。*

blocks.en: *Filled in by [arena](../../arena/SKILL.md). Records which candidate became the base and why, what was adapted from each of the others, and what was rejected and why.*
blocks.zh: *由 [arena](../../arena/SKILL.md) 填写。记录哪份候选成为基底及原因，从其余候选吸收了什么，以及拒绝了什么、为什么。*

blocks.en: *One bullet per tradeoff the chosen shape makes. Form: "we accept X in exchange for Y." Name anything a future reader might mistake for an oversight, including things that look like premature optimization or premature simplification.*
blocks.zh: *每项权衡一条，形式为“我们接受 X，以换取 Y”。列出未来读者可能误以为遗漏的内容，包括看起来像过早优化或过早简化的选择。*

blocks.en: *Required. Name at least one concrete alternative shape, with one line on why it lost. Judge each alternative on interface depth, not implementation simplicity alone. Name the complexity it exposes to callers and the complexity it hides. Two or three alternatives belong here when the design space had real contenders. One is fine when the constraints forced the answer, with the conclusion phrased as "this was the only viable shape because..." Avoid listing flavors of the same shape. This section covers design alternatives the chosen shape considered and rejected, not other runner candidates.*
blocks.zh: *必填。至少一个具体替代形态，用一行说明未采用原因。评价每个方案的接口深度，不只看实现是否简单；说明暴露给调用方与隐藏的复杂性。设计空间中确有竞争方案时，列两三个。约束迫使答案唯一时，一个也可以，结论写为“这是唯一可行形态，因为……”。避免列同一形态的小变种。此节说明被选形态考虑并拒绝的设计替代方案，不是其他 runner 候选。*

blocks.en: *Things you noticed during the sketch that the human needs to weigh in on, and risks worth flagging before implementation starts. Phrase as questions, not assertions, so the human's answer is the resolution rather than a comment.*
blocks.zh: *画草图时发现、需要用户权衡的事项，以及实现前值得提醒的风险。写成问题，不写成断言，让用户答案成为解决方式，而非旁注。*

blocks.en: *The first thing to build against the sketch. One sentence. What you'd start writing immediately after synthesis (or after Phase D sign-off, if a checkpoint was opted into).*
blocks.zh: *针对草图首先构建什么，用一句话说明。综合完成后（或选择检查点时，在 Phase D 确认后），你会立刻开始写什么。*
